notes: Eval 1 (feature integration) does not discriminate: all 6 runs, with or without a skill, passed all 7 assertions and the evaluator's acceptance script. Haiku 5.5 solves this fixture unaided; a harder fixture is needed.

Largest skill effect is eval 4 (a 'trivial' rename): both no-skill runs skipped re-reading the edited file and never used the project's documented test runner (one ran no tests); all 4 skill runs (v1.1 and v2.0) did both.
Eval 2: both no-skill runs and one v1.1 run left __pycache__ in a project the user said not to change; neither v2.0 run did. This is a strict reading of 'don't change anything'.

Eval 3: all 6 runs answered correctly (exit 5, from 3.12). Differences are in the CI advice. One no-skill run had the best sourcing (3.12.0b1 NEWS entry, verified). One v1.1 run found the 3.12.0/3.12.1 vs 3.12.3 skip-condition change (verified). The other v1.1 run misread the 3.13 docs.
Cost: v2.0 vs v1.1 is -12% tokens, -17% wall time and -35% tool calls. v2.0 vs no skill is +24% tokens and +38% wall time.
Not asserted: unrequested docs/formats.md edits in eval 1 happened in no-skill 1/2, v1.1 2/2 and v2.0 1/2 runs. Neither skill version prevents this scope creep.
Caveats: n=2 per cell. The grader also wrote v2.0, and grading was not blind. v2.0 beats v1.1 on only two assertion outcomes, which is not statistically meaningful.
